x: Oscar Horwood has been another victm to illness and was unable to be present at Wimbledon for the Horwood Cup Race. Likewise Teddy Gordon, who is now recuperating near Bristol.

Frank Elson helped with a football scheme, Tom Cotton, Teddy Gordon, Wally Bayliss and others contributed their ideas, a Smoking Concert was held at the old mid-week quarters and still our Building Fund, as it was now called, grew.

Teddy Gordon sends best wishes to all members. We regret to report the illness of Oscar Horwood and we send wishes for a speedy recovery and assure him we do still remember his wonderful work for the Club thirty years ago.

The winners of the team race were Bristol A.C., which was a just reward for their long journey, and who should be with them but our old past President, Teddy Gordon, and you can imagine his pleasure at their success and in our getting third.

Teddy Gordon provided some building brick money boxes in which the surplus halfpennies could be placed each evening. Frank Elson came along with a scheme based on football results which added to our funds and was succeeded by a more ambitious scheme still, organised by Frank Elson and Tom Cotton and…

With Teddy Gordon's aid, wooden money boxes were made, called Belgrave Bricks, and these were distributed to nearly all members. In announcing the scheme's inauguration Harry Hare said "This scheme will not cost you a penny".
